title: Sausage Casserole
subtitle: Pork sausages braised in a rich tomato and bean sauce
excerpt: Pork sausages browned and braised with onion, pepper, cannellini beans, and tinned tomatoes in a thick, smoky sauce. A one-pot weeknight supper that improves on reheating.

recipe.sourceNotes: Sausage casserole is a British weeknight staple. Unlike the French cassoulet from which it draws loose inspiration, the British version is quicker, less laboured, and built around supermarket pork sausages rather than preserved meats and confit duck. The technique is straightforward: brown the sausages first for flavour, then braise everything together. Cannellini beans or borlotti beans are the most common addition. The dish is forgiving and freezes well.

content.text: Brown the sausages well before adding the other ingredients: this develops the flavour and gives the casserole depth. Simmer on the lowest heat possible for the full cooking time so the sausages stay tender and the sauce thickens gradually without scorching. Serve with crusty bread or mashed potato.
Heat the oil in a large, heavy-based pan over medium-high heat. Brown the sausages on all sides, about 6 minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, fry the onion and pepper over medium heat for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, tomato paste, and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute.

Add the tinned tomatoes, cannellini beans, thyme, and bay leaves. Return the sausages. Season. Bring to a simmer. Cook over low heat for 25 to 30 minutes until the sauce is thick. Serve with crusty bread or mashed potato.
